title: Accurate measurement of cytosolic free zinc using eCALWY variants: a toolbox of genetically encoded FRET sensors
protocol: Plate the cells on glass coverslips typically 72 hours prior to the experiment.
Wait until the cells reach 40-60% confluency within 24 hours.
Transfect the cells with 1 microg of plasmid DNA using Lipofectamine™ 2000 according to the manufacturer's instructions, 48 hours before imaging.
Prepare 5 ml per coverslip of KHBP without additives.
Prepare 5 ml per coverslip of KHBP containing an agent that perturbs or activates Zn<sup>2+</sup> pathways.
Prepare 5 ml per coverslip of KHBP with 50 microM TPEN.
Prepare two separate 5 ml solutions per coverslip of KHBP without additives to prevent cross-contamination.
Prepare 5 ml per coverslip of KHBP containing 5 microM pyrithione and 100 microM ZnCl<sub>2</sub>.
Place all buffers in a waterbath at 37°C.
Re-bubble KHBP with 95% air/5% CO<sub>2</sub> for 10 minutes every 2 hours to control CO<sub>2</sub> levels.
Measure the time elapsed between the buffer entering the perifusion tubing and reaching the outlet.
Take glass coverslips with transfected eCALWY variant of interest from the incubator.
Mount the coverslips into a 3.5-cm imaging chamber.
Add 1 ml of KHBP to the cells in the imaging chamber.
Mount the inlet and outlet of the perifusion system to the imaging chamber.
Ensure that the outlet is at a higher level than the inlet.
Ensure that the outlet flow is at least equal to the inlet.
Focus on the cells using brightfield illumination.
Switch to fluorescence illumination to choose a field of view.
Preferably, select multiple cells in one field of view.
Evaluate different intensities of expression levels of the indicator.
Confirm that the expression level of the indicator does not affect the cytosolic zinc level.
Evaluate the localization of the sensor.
Ensure that cells appear healthy.
Start perifusion with regular KHBP.
Adjust the flow to ensure constant buffer flow over the cells without dislodging them.
Start image acquisition.
Acquire images every 1 or 2 seconds to obtain binding and release kinetics data.
Incubate with KHBP containing no additives for 2 minutes.
Incubate with KHBP containing an agent that perturbs or activates Zn<sup>2+</sup> influx or efflux pathways until steady-state Zn<sup>2+</sup> levels are reached.
Incubate with KHBP containing no additives for 2 minutes.
Incubate with 50 microM TPEN in KHBP for 3 minutes to determine R<sub>max</sub>.
Incubate with 5 microM pyrithione and 100 microM ZnCl<sub>2</sub> in KHBP for 2 minutes to determine R<sub>min</sub>.
Rinse the perifusion tubing with KHBP after each experiment.
Select regions of interest (ROIs) for analysis.
Draw an ROI in individual fluorescent cells.
Include an ROI for background correction, preferably a non-transfected cell or empty area.
Use identical ROIs for FRET and CFP images at each time point.
Calculate the average intensity in each ROI.
Export the data in ASCII or another format.
Import the exported data into a data processing program like Microsoft Excel.
Calculate the FRET ratio for each timepoint using the provided equation.
Generate background-corrected ratio images using ImageJ via the RatioPlus plugin.
Convert sensor occupancy into Zn<sup>2+</sup> concentration using the formula: \[Zn<sup>2+</sup>] = (\(R_{max} - R\) / \(R - R_{min}\)) * K<sub>d\).
Plot FRET ratio changes and \[Zn<sup>2+</sup>\] on time traces with left and right vertical axes for the two calibrations.
Report exact parameters used for conversion to \[Zn<sup>2+</sup>\].
Repeat steps 3-9 with each of the eCALWY variants using the following timeframe:
Mix KHBP containing no additives for 2 minutes.
Mix KHBP containing 50 microM TPEN for 3 minutes to determine R_max.
Mix KHBP containing 5 microM pyrithione and 100 microM ZnCl₂ for 2 minutes to determine R_min.
Rinse the perifusion tubing with KHBP after each experiment if multiple coverslips are measured sequentially to prevent saturation with Zn²⁺ at the start of the next experiment.
Repeat steps 10-11 for all eCALWY variants.
Calculate the sensor occupancy at resting Zn²⁺ levels using the equation:
Occupancy (%) = ((R_max - R_rest) / (R_max - R_min)) * 100
